summary: Apple has officially taken over the independent iCloud Passwords add-on for Firefox, transitioning its ownership on addons.mozilla.org from developer Aurélien Garnier to Apple Inc. This move allows Firefox users running macOS Sonoma or recent Windows versions to confidently use Apple's password management features outside of Safari. Masimo alleges that former CEO Joe Kiani and RTW conspired to manipulate shareholder votes, rigging 19% in Kiani's favor through practices like put options or selling shares after record dates. While empty voting is not inherently illegal, Masimo claims evidence of an insider group, which is a red flag for the SEC and potentially the Department of Justice. | Apple has significantly expanded its footprint at 11 Penn Plaza in Midtown Manhattan, securing an additional 61,000 square feet and bringing its total occupancy to 460,000 square feet. This deal, a direct lease agreement with Vornado Realty Trust rather than a sublease from Macy's, allows Apple to occupy floors four through fourteen of the historic building. Despite Apple's expansion, Macy's remains the primary tenant and headquarters at 11 Penn Plaza. | This article delves into Apple's strategy for generative AI, dubbed Apple Intelligence, highlighting the company's "best, not first" approach. Key executives, including John Giannandrea and Craig Federighi, explain that Apple has been preparing for this moment for years and focused on integrating AI at a systems level with a strong emphasis on privacy. The piece also contrasts Apple's approach with competitors and discusses the future trajectory of AI at Apple. | Apple is preparing to launch its own series of cellular modem chips starting next year, aiming to replace components from Qualcomm by 2027. This move intensifies competition with Qualcomm, which currently supplies modems to Apple, and could impact other Apple suppliers like Skyworks Solutions and Qorvo. Apple has been developing its own modem technology since acquiring Intel's modem unit in 2019 and recently signed a deal with Broadcom for 5G radio frequency components. | BlackRock, Inc. reduced its stake in the iShares MSCI Poland ETF (EPOL) by selling 880,171 shares on November 30, 2024, at $22.09 per share, leaving them with 133,296 shares. This move reflects a strategic adjustment by BlackRock, a leading investment firm with $4.761.03 trillion in equity and top holdings like Apple and Amazon. Produced by TSMC, Sinope offers download speeds of up to 4 gigabits per second, which is less than half of Qualcomm's latest modems due to more limited frequency support and carrier aggregation implementation. Apple plans to integrate Sinope with its Carpo RF front end and aims to release more advanced custom modems in subsequent years, eventually hoping to outperform Qualcomm and integrate modems directly into iPhone processors, as well as extend their use to Macs and the Vision Pro.

summary: Gartner has announced its list of the top 10 strategic technology trends for 2025, which organizations should explore. This project, which involved cross-border collaboration and a tight deadline, marks the beginning of a new client relationship with Invesco Real Estate and represents one of their largest commercial real estate loans in Europe in 2024. James Moy, Head of EMEA Valuation at Colliers, led the team in delivering high-quality valuation advice. | This article highlights Constellation Energy (CEG) and Dominion Energy (D) as two promising AI stocks for investing in the future of energy, driven by increasing global electricity demand and strategic partnerships with Magnificent Seven companies. Both companies are expanding their carbon-free electricity generation, including nuclear and renewables, to meet the rising power needs primarily from data centers and other AI-driven technologies. The company's Trusted AI initiative and product enhancements, like VantageCloud Lake and ClearScape Analytics, aim to provide reliable and actionable insights for businesses. This move signals a shift from the previous "Work Your Way" flexible policy implemented under the former CEO. The change, starting next month at the Maplewood headquarters and expanding globally, aims to "reinvigorate the 3M innovation machine" amidst a period of sluggish growth and legal setbacks.

title: Equinix is closing its bare metal IaaS platform | This Insurance Giant Has Cut Its Office Budget By $244 Million in 4 Years — Here's Where Employees Will Meet Instead | Mattel Bets Big On Its IP | OneAscent Large Cap Core ETF Holdings | Costco Membership Fees Are What Makes It Profitable | Allstate Thinks Outside the Cubicle With Flexible Workspaces | Qurate’s new strategy banks on streaming, social media platforms | $12.5M financing completed for iconic Culver Theater in California | Wall Street’s hottest stock, Palantir, only employs 3,892 people
summary: Equinix announced it will discontinue its bare-metal infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS) platform, Equinix Metal, by June 2026. The decision comes due to the platform representing only 1.25% of the company's revenue and intense competition from hyperscalers like AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud. Equinix will continue to prioritize performance, security, and stability features until the sunset date and assist customers with transitioning to alternative solutions. | Allstate has significantly cut its annual spending on corporate offices by $244 million over four years, reducing its real estate footprint from 12 million square feet to 4 million. To accommodate its workforce, Allstate is implementing a new strategy where 25% of its 54,000 corporate employees will utilize coworking spaces for meetings and team-building, a less strict approach compared to companies like Amazon and Dell. This "testing and learning" phase allows the insurance giant to manage in-person gatherings in cities where a full office lease isn't necessary. | Mattel Inc. is shifting its strategy to heavily capitalize on its intellectual property by expanding into movies, TV shows, and theme parks. This move, spearheaded by CEO Ynon Kreiz, aims to leverage iconic brands like Barbie and Hot Wheels beyond traditional toy sales, creating new revenue streams and engaging adult fans. The strategy appears to be paying off, with significant net income growth and positive analyst outlooks, despite the company's stock price being lower than its all-time high. | The OneAscent Large Cap Core ETF (OALC), established in 2021, focuses on large-cap equity, managing $231.6 million in assets across 206 holdings. Its portfolio is actively managed, screened for value-based philosophy, and aims for capital appreciation. Key holdings include NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Amazon. | Costco's membership fees, while only 2% of annual revenue, are crucial to its profitability because they contribute 66% of the retailer's bottom line due to their presumed zero cost. The company recently raised its membership fees for the first time in seven years, impacting 52 million members. This move significantly boosts Costco's net income, which rose 17% to $7.37 billion in the last fiscal year. | Allstate is embracing flexible workspaces, moving beyond traditional offices to a hybrid model that includes coworking spaces and redesigned leased offices. This shift aims to reduce real estate costs and offer employees more collaborative and focused environments, acknowledging that the pandemic has permanently changed white-collar work. The company is using platforms like LiquidSpace for on-demand offices, adapting to the needs of a remote-first workforce while still providing opportunities for in-person interaction. | Qurate Retail Group, parent company of QVC and HSN, is rebranding to QVC Group and shifting its focus to live social shopping across streaming and social media platforms. The company aims to generate $1.5 billion in revenue from these new channels within three years, despite recent struggles with falling sales and Nasdaq compliance issues. This strategic pivot includes leadership changes and a push to tailor content for platforms like TikTok, Facebook, YouTube, Netflix, and Hulu. | JLL Capital Markets has successfully arranged $12.5 million in senior financing for the Culver Theater in Culver City, California. The financing for the 41,341-square-foot movie theater and production studio was secured for Oliver McMillan LLC through Zions Capital Markets. This prime real estate asset, located in a thriving hub for media and technology, is 100% occupied and benefits from a long-term lease with a global e-commerce giant. | Palantir (PLTR) has become the S&P 500's best-performing stock, reaching a $150 billion market capitalization despite having fewer than 4,000 employees. The company's shares surged after strong third-quarter earnings, driven by demand for its AI platform, and a planned move to Nasdaq. This remarkable valuation highlights a growing trend in AI-adjacent stocks where market cap per employee is a significant metric.

summary: Southern California Edison (SCE) and NVIDIA have partnered in what they call the "Intelligent Grid Collaboration" to address the rapidly increasing demand for electricity, which is projected to grow 35% faster than previously estimated. This collaboration aims to develop AI and other technology solutions to make the electric grid more intelligent, autonomous, and adaptive, focusing on enhancing customer load interconnection, improving inspections, and optimizing incident management. The initiative seeks to accelerate affordable decarbonization and electrification, with pilot project demonstrations expected within the year. | Crusoe Energy Systems is collaborating with Vast Data to provide high-performance AI storage, called "Shared Disks," to its Crusoe Cloud customers, offering petabyte-scale file systems with high read/write bandwidth and a 99.5 percent SLA. Additionally, Crusoe is partnering with SES AI Corporation to accelerate material discovery for batteries using Crusoe's AI cloud and Nvidia H100 virtualized instances, aiming to map the molecular universe and improve energy storage solutions. This dual collaboration highlights Crusoe's pivot to AI data centers powered by sustainable energy and its commitment to driving innovation in both AI infrastructure and material science. | Planet Labs PBC has released the first "light" images from its Tanager-1 hyperspectral satellite, demonstrating its capability to capture detailed spectral data for various applications including environmental monitoring and defense. Concurrently, BAE Systems' prototype payload, featuring an RF sounder and SWIR camera, has been integrated onto the International Space Station, aiming to advance environmental monitoring and weather forecasting technologies. Both initiatives highlight significant advancements in Earth observation and space-based data collection. | Global technology distributor Ingram Micro, owned by Platinum Equity, has filed for an Initial Public Offering (IPO) with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, signaling its return to public markets. The company plans to list its common stock on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol "INGM" and intends to use the proceeds to repay outstanding loans. This move follows the company generating $48.1 billion in global net sales in 2023 and working with numerous partners and MSPs. | This article discusses two ETFs, the Subversive Unusual Whales Democratic ETF (BATS: NANC) and the Subversive Unusual Whales Republican ETF (BATS: KRUZ), which track the stock trades of U.S. members of Congress. The NANC ETF, heavily invested in technology stocks like NVIDIA and Microsoft, has seen a 50% increase since its inception, while the KRUZ ETF, with a more diversified approach including financial and industrial sectors, has risen 25%. Both ETFs offer investors a way to potentially benefit from the "insider knowledge" of Congress members regarding government and legislative impacts on the stock market. | Snowflake's stock (SNOW) has fallen significantly despite strong revenue growth in its cloud data warehousing business. The article suggests that if Snowflake's revenues grow by 3.5x between FY'24 and FY'27 and its price-to-sales multiple remains around 10x, the stock could reach over $300, representing a nearly 3x upside. This projection is based on the company's leadership in cloud data warehousing, its potential to benefit from generative AI, and an expanding total addressable market. | Poolside Inc., an AI coding startup, has secured $500 million in a Series B funding round, bringing its total raised capital to $626 million and valuing the company at $3 billion. The company, co-founded by former GitHub CTO Jason Warner, is developing generative AI coding assistants that utilize reinforcement learning to continuously improve, aiming to compete with existing solutions like GitHub Copilot. Poolside plans to use the new funds for R&D, go-to-market initiatives, and purchasing 10,000 Nvidia GPUs to train future models, emphasizing its ambition to achieve artificial general intelligence in software development. | Adam Auerbach from EPAM Systems argues that engineers should view AI as a collaborative tool rather than a competitor. He emphasizes that AI, through tools like Microsoft Copilot and AI Agents, can automate tedious tasks and accelerate the software development lifecycle, allowing engineers to focus on higher-value activities. The article stresses the importance of training, change management, and prompt library platforms for successful AI integration within engineering teams. | Cantor Fitzgerald has upgraded Teradyne, Inc. (TER) to Overweight, adding it to their Top Picks list due to its strong leverage to AI, networking, high bandwidth memory, and custom silicon. The upgrade also highlights Teradyne's potential for recovery in broader industry sectors like auto and industrial test, and its strong positioning in the robotics and mobile markets. The article contextualizes this decision within the massive ongoing investments in AI infrastructure, including specialized hardware, data centers, and cloud computing. | AES, a clean energy leader and top dividend stock, is seeing increased demand for its services due to the AI-fueled growth in data centers. The company operates power plants, electricity grids, and energy storage facilities globally, making it a compelling choice for climate-conscious investors. This surge in demand highlights AES's strategic position in the evolving energy landscape.

summary: Microsoft and Rezolve AI have announced a strategic partnership to bring AI-powered commerce solutions to retailers globally. It details how organizations can better quantify the value of enterprise apps to secure funding, align strategy with business outcomes, and leverage AI and automation for agility. This initiative has consolidated 40 legacy systems into one, reduced change control steps from 11 to 5, and enabled 60% of deviations to be fast-tracked, significantly improving efficiency and data integrity. The company aims to deliver innovative treatments to patients faster by digitizing and standardizing processes. | Andre-Philippe Hardy, head of Canadian research at TD Securities, has identified Brookfield Renewable Partners L.P., Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC), and Celestica Inc. as his top Canadian stock picks. He expects consumer burdens from high interest rates to ease with predicted rate cuts. Hardy highlights Brookfield Renewable for its role in clean energy for data centers, CIBC for its growth and strong capitalization, and Celestica for its essential infrastructure support for the AI industry.

summary: Gartner has announced its list of the top 10 strategic technology trends for 2025, which organizations should explore. These trends encompass AI imperatives and risks, new frontiers of computing, and human-machine synergy, aiming to help IT leaders shape the future of their organizations responsibly. Key trends include Agentic AI, AI Governance Platforms, Disinformation Security, Postquantum Cryptography, Ambient Invisible Intelligence, Energy-Efficient Computing, Hybrid Computing, Spatial Computing, Polyfunctional Robots, and Neurological Enhancement. | Rackspace Technology achieved $40 million in total cost of ownership savings by migrating from SPLA to Azure Arc. This pivot optimized SQL licensing, improved Extended Security Updates delivery, and enhanced hybrid cloud operations, resulting in increased reporting proficiency and customer satisfaction. The company aims for 80% growth in Azure Arc consumption within the next three years, leveraging Azure Arc for unified management and new cloud services. | This article highlights Constellation Energy (CEG) and Dominion Energy (D) as two promising AI stocks for investing in the future of energy, driven by increasing global electricity demand and strategic partnerships with Magnificent Seven companies. Both companies are expanding their carbon-free electricity generation, including nuclear and renewables, to meet the rising power needs primarily from data centers and other AI-driven technologies. The article details their recent financial performance, analyst ratings, and their strategic initiatives, such as CEG's 20-year power agreement with Microsoft and D's MOU with Amazon Web Services for small modular nuclear reactors. | Dow Jones and The New York Post have filed a copyright and trademark infringement lawsuit against AI startup Perplexity. The lawsuit alleges that Perplexity not only violates copyright but also "hallucinates" fake news sections, attributing them to legitimate publishers, thereby damaging their reputation and confusing readers. This action follows similar cease-and-desist letters sent to Perplexity by other news organizations, including The New York Times and WIRED, regarding the unauthorized use and misrepresentation of their content. | Cisco has confirmed a security incident after a hacker, 'IntelBroker', offered to sell data allegedly stolen from the company. The networking giant stated that a small number of unauthorized files were published from a public-facing DevHub environment, but its core systems were not breached. The company is investigating but has not found sensitive PII or financial data among the stolen files. | Two Indian-origin CEOs, Nikesh Arora of Palo Alto Networks Inc and Satya Nadella of Microsoft Corp, are among the top 10 highest-paid S&P 500 company leaders. Arora ranks second with over $151 million, while Nadella is tenth with over $48 million. This highlights a significant disparity between CEO pay, which has surged by over $4 million in a decade, and the average US worker's wage increase of $18,240 during the same period. | IBM has released the latest version of its AI models, "Granite 3.0," for businesses, making them open-source to compete in the generative AI market. This strategy contrasts with rivals like Microsoft, which charge for access, while IBM offers a paid tool, Watsonx, for running customized models. These new models, trained on Nvidia's H100 GPUs, will be available on the Watsonx platform and Nvidia's software tools. | Teradata emphasizes the critical role of trusted data and scalable AI in driving enterprise innovation and decision-making. The company's Trusted AI initiative and product enhancements, like VantageCloud Lake and ClearScape Analytics, aim to provide reliable and actionable insights for businesses. Teradata also focuses on open integration with major cloud providers and tools, ensuring flexibility and synergy in AI deployment, as demonstrated by a retail project that achieved a 28% sales uplift.

summary: Apple announced a new iMac featuring the powerful M4 chip and Apple Intelligence, boasting significant performance improvements and new features. This updated iMac comes in a range of new colors, offers a nano-texture display option, an enhanced 12MP Center Stage camera, and improved Thunderbolt 4 connectivity. It starts at $1,299, with pre-orders available immediately and shipping beginning November 8, promising a transformative user experience with AI capabilities and privacy protections. | Numerous supply-side partners, including FreeWheel, Index Exchange, Magnite, Microsoft Monetize, and PubMatic, are integrating the European Unified ID (EUID). This open-source identity solution, developed by The Trade Desk, aims to help marketers and publishers maintain relevant advertising in Europe, particularly as the industry moves beyond third-party cookies. EUID utilizes hashed email addresses and encrypted identifiers for a privacy-conscious, interoperable identity framework. | NextEra Energy (NYSE: NEE) is showing strong performance in 2024, outperforming the S&P 500 with a 39% total return, driven by its diverse business segments including rate-regulated utilities and competitive market energy sales. The company benefits from a substantial backlog of renewable energy projects and is exploring recommissioning nuclear assets like the Duane Arnold plant, capitalizing on rising energy demand, particularly from data centers. NextEra's varied approach to energy generation, which includes natural gas, nuclear, wind, and solar, positions it for continued growth as U.S. electricity demand is projected to rise significantly. | Nvidia briefly surpassed Apple to become the world's most valuable company, driven by the immense demand for its specialized AI chips crucial for advanced AI applications. This shift highlights the growing importance of AI-driven technologies in the tech market, with Nvidia benefiting significantly from the race among tech giants to dominate AI. While Apple later regained its lead, Nvidia's surge underscores the impact of AI on market valuations and investment trends. | ResMed, known for its CPAP devices, is leveraging its vast sleep and breathing data to expand into new markets using AI, generative AI, and machine learning. The company's proprietary digital health dataset, including 20 billion nights of sleep data, positions it to address 2.3 billion people with sleep and breathing disorders and venture into areas like insomnia and COPD. ResMed is also using AI to drive productivity internally with its Dawn generative AI assistant and plans to integrate with consumer wearable data to personalize patient care. | Asset managers are launching new exchange-traded funds (ETFs) focused on artificial intelligence to capitalize on the growing market enthusiasm for AI technologies. Over a third of AI-themed ETFs have been introduced in 2024 alone, bringing the total assets in this category to $4.5 billion. This proliferation comes as venture capital firms are also significantly increasing their investment in AI startups, with projections of $79.2 billion by year-end. | MoneyGram International, Inc. has appointed Anthony Soohoo as its new Chief Executive Officer, effective immediately. Mr. Soohoo, an experienced technology executive with a background in digital transformations, succeeds Alex Holmes, who will transition to an advisory role. His focus will be on executing MoneyGram's digital innovation strategy and expanding its global partner network, leveraging his extensive experience in technology, business, and artificial intelligence. | US-based solar developer Sunrun is in discussions with several data center developers to supply their facilities with distributed solar power. Sunrun is exploring models to provide bespoke solar systems or leverage existing community solar systems for data centers, reflecting the growing demand for clean energy in the data center industry. This move aligns with the exponential growth of the US solar market and increasing efforts by data centers to secure renewable energy sources. | As businesses face a growing talent crunch, traditional hiring methods are proving insufficient. This article discusses leveraging AI and globalization to access diverse global talent pools, address skill gaps, and achieve sustainable growth. It highlights how technology can streamline global hiring, manage complexities, and foster diverse, globally distributed workforces while emphasizing the importance of employee well-being and cultural sensitivity. | AI investment continues to surge, prompting asset management companies to launch new ETFs focused on artificial intelligence. Over a third of the more than 20 AI-named ETFs were released this year, with their combined assets reaching $4.5 billion. Major tech companies like Microsoft and Amazon are engaging in an "AI arms race," significantly increasing capital expenditure in the sector, while venture capital funding for AI startups is also seeing a substantial boost.

summary: COPT Defense Properties is planning a 1GW data center campus near Des Moines, Iowa, after acquiring a 365-acre land parcel for $32 million. The campus is projected to include 15 buildings totaling 3.3 million square feet and will serve an existing Fortune 100 cloud computing tenant. This expansion leverages Des Moines' attractive land values, power availability, renewable energy access, and tax incentives. | Despite an 8% sell-off following strong Q4 2024 results and a guidance raise, Seagate Technology Holdings PLC presents a buy-the-dip opportunity for investors. The article highlights motivations such as potentially low-balled forecasts for Q2 2025, increasing demand for HDDs due to video and GenAI content, and the competitive advantage of Seagate's HAMR technology for AI data centers. Technical analysis also suggests a bullish ascending triangle pattern for STX shares. | Alphabet announced strong Q3 2024 results, exceeding market expectations for revenue and adjusted EPS. The company reported $88.27 billion in revenue, a 15.1% growth, and an impressive operating profit increase of 33.7%, reaching $28.52 billion. The Cloud segment showed significant acceleration with nearly 35% year-over-year revenue growth, and CEO Sundar Pichai highlighted AI as a key driver for future growth across its core segments like search and YouTube. | Gail Evans, a distinguished executive who held leadership roles at Eastman Kodak, Bank of America, HP, Microsoft, Mercer, and Disney, passed away on October 29, 2024, at the age of 65. Born in Rochester, NY, she diligently pursued education, earning degrees from Hobart William Smith, Nazareth University, and the University of Rochester. Evans was celebrated for her professional achievements and her dedication to her family, leaving behind a legacy of warmth, joy, and purpose. | Pegasystems Inc. announced the general availability of Pega Infinity 24.2, introducing new generative AI capabilities to boost productivity and optimize customer experiences. The updates enhance solutions like Pega Platform, Pega Customer Decision Hub, Pega Customer Service, and Pega Sales Automation. These improvements enable enterprises to accelerate application development, engage customers with contextualized experiences, and automate workflows more efficiently through advanced AI integration. | Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) shares tumbled by over 6% in after-hours trading despite narrowly beating Wall Street expectations for earnings and revenue in Q3 2024. The company reported record Data Center revenue, but analysts noted that its new AI chip announcements don't significantly close the gap with Nvidia. AMD's stock had more than doubled since early 2023 due to high demand for AI chips.

summary: Microsoft has been recognized as a Leader in the 2024 Gartner Magic Quadrant for B2B Marketing Automation Platforms for Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights for the third consecutive year. This recognition highlights Microsoft's advancements in leveraging data, AI, and automation to deliver personalized customer experiences, particularly through innovations like Copilot and unified customer data across sales, marketing, and service functions. The framework, an outgrowth of SEI’s AI Center of Excellence, is currently being used by approximately 400 employees for tasks like client service, process automation, and contract analysis. Investors are encouraged to consider VGT for long-term portfolio growth, possibly employing a dollar-cost averaging strategy to mitigate volatility. | Despite U.S. stocks, particularly those linked to AI, continuing to reach new highs, international stocks have shown even stronger performance, with the MSCI All Country World ex USA Index up significantly. It lists top holdings like NVIDIA, Apple, and Microsoft, and provides a comprehensive log of recent changes in its portfolio.

title: Day 1 | With its new AI shopping assistant, Canadian Tire wants to take the friction out of buying tires | AI impact at Dow: Copilot identifies millions in cost savings | Warren Buffett Owns 1 Vanguard Index Fund That Could Soar by 150%, According to a Top Wall Street Analyst | Amazon, IKEA join other ocean cargo shippers to boost demand for new green fuels | SK Telecom to acquire additional 24.76% stake in SK Broadband | Broadcom’s VMware strategy is winning despite market friction
summary: The SLB Digital Forum 2024 Day One focused on the urgent need for digital transformation in the energy industry, emphasizing the role of AI, partnerships, and resilient infrastructure. Key highlights included the launch of the AI-powered Lumi platform and discussions from industry leaders like ADNOC, ENI, and AWS on navigating new frontiers, sustainability, and scaling digital solutions. The forum stressed moving from proof-of-concept to full-scale deployment to achieve a higher-value, lower-carbon future. | Canadian Tire has launched CeeTee, an AI-powered shopping assistant developed with Microsoft, to simplify the tire buying process for customers. Available through the Canadian Tire app, CeeTee helps customers choose tires by asking questions, providing options, and checking stock. This initiative aims to enhance the customer experience and potentially increase Canadian Tire's market share in the complex tire category. | Dow partnered with Microsoft to use Copilot and AI agents to transform its freight invoicing system, aiming to identify and rectify billing inaccuracies in its multi-billion dollar annual shipping operations. By automating the analysis of thousands of invoices, the company anticipates saving millions of dollars in shipping costs annually, demonstrating a significant advancement in operational efficiency through AI. This initiative serves as a playbook for other organizations looking to harness AI to solve complex business problems, starting with identifying major pain points and leveraging organizational data. | Warren Buffett, through Berkshire Hathaway, holds positions in two S&P 500-tracking ETFs, with the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF being highlighted for its low expense ratio. A top Wall Street analyst, Tom Lee of Fundstrat Global Advisors, predicts the S&P 500 could rise by 150% by 2030, driven by demographic shifts and the AI boom. The article emphasizes Buffett's advice for retail investors to opt for index funds over stock picking. | Amazon, IKEA, and about three dozen other companies are forming an alliance called the Zero Emissions Maritime Buyers Alliance to boost demand for new green e-fuels in ocean shipping. The alliance will invite shipping firms to bid on contracts in January for cargo movement on vessels powered by near-zero emissions e-fuels like e-methanol, aiming to accelerate the industry's move toward net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. These three- to five-year contracts, starting in 2027, are estimated to abate approximately 470,000 metric tons of GHG emissions. | SK Telecom plans to acquire an additional 24.76 percent stake in its subsidiary SK Broadband from Taekwang Group and Mirae Asset Financial Group for 1.15 trillion won by May 2025. This acquisition will increase SKT's stake in SK Broadband to 99.1 percent, aiming to strengthen its presence in data centers and submarine cable investments to advance its AI capabilities. The move is part of SKT's broader strategy to invest heavily in the AI sector and enhance operational efficiency across all business sectors. | Broadcom's acquisition of VMware is succeeding despite media and competitor narratives focusing on increased license fees. The strategy involves narrowing VMware's focus, increasing contract values through the VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) bundle, and integrating VMware into Broadcom’s business model. While some customers are migrating low-value workloads, most mission-critical work remains, leading to significant revenue increases and a long-term win for customers, competitors, and Broadcom.

title: How to mitigate wiper malware
summary: Wiper malware, referred to as wiperware, is a dangerous form of cyberattack that leads to the complete destruction of data and systems, making recovery nearly impossible. Unlike ransomware, which often has a profit motive, wiperware is primarily used for sabotage, psychological fear, and to erase evidence of an attack. This article details the impact of wiperware on businesses and provides strategies for mitigation, including regular, immutable backups, securing email, applying patches, using MFA and zero trust, and securing endpoints.

summary: NVIDIA and SoftBank Corp. are collaborating to accelerate Japan's sovereign AI initiatives, with SoftBank building Japan's most powerful AI supercomputer using NVIDIA's Blackwell platform and planning for the Grace Blackwell platform. They have also successfully piloted the world's first combined AI and 5G telecom network using NVIDIA AI Aerial, creating new revenue opportunities for telecom operators. SoftBank is also developing an AI marketplace with NVIDIA AI Enterprise to meet Japan's demand for local and secure AI computing. | NVIDIA announced that several prominent Japanese cloud providers, including SoftBank Corp., GMO Internet Group, Highreso, KDDI, Rutilea, and SAKURA Internet, are adopting NVIDIA's accelerated computing, networking, and software to build AI infrastructure. These initiatives are supported by the Japan Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) and aim to transform industries such as robotics, automotive, healthcare, and telecommunications for the age of AI. The cloud services will leverage NVIDIA technologies like Blackwell platforms, H200 Tensor Core GPUs, and HGX systems across various regions in Japan. | NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang and SoftBank CEO Masayoshi Son discussed Japan's pivotal role in the AI revolution at NVIDIA's AI Summit Japan. Huang emphasized that every industry and country needs a new industrial revolution driven by AI, with Japan uniquely positioned to lead in both digital (agentic AI) and physical (robotics AI) domains. A major announcement included NVIDIA's collaboration with SoftBank to build Japan's most powerful AI supercomputer using the NVIDIA Blackwell platform to support sovereign AI initiatives. | The article highlights that a little-known chip-equipment company, Camtek, benefits from the significant increase in AI investment, especially from Nvidia's data center hardware sales. Camtek supplies key Nvidia partners like TSMC, SK Hynix, and Micron, indicating that the AI boom creates substantial opportunities beyond Nvidia itself. This suggests that the financial gains from AI investment are distributed among various players in the semiconductor supply chain. | This article argues that investors should consider investing in both value and growth stocks, rather than exclusively one or the other. It highlights the historically high concentration in equity markets driven by a few large growth stocks, elevated growth valuations, and the potential for a market leadership change where value could outperform. The authors suggest that diversification is key to mitigate risk and that combining value and growth strategies makes sense. | Monolithic Power Systems confirmed in calls with analysts that it remains in NVIDIA Corporation's bill of materials for its next-generation systems and has no performance issues. The company also stated that its Q4-2024 guidance remains unchanged. This news comes amidst various analyst ratings and observations regarding MPWR's market position. | The Schwab U.S. Large-Cap ETF (SCHX) is highlighted as a compelling investment option due to its low expense ratio (0.03%), broad diversification across large-cap U.S. equities, and strong recent performance. It tracks approximately 750 of the largest publicly-traded U.S. stocks, with significant weight in tech giants like Apple, Microsoft, and Nvidia. The article discusses both the potential for continued outperformance in large-cap stocks and the inherent market risks, especially concerning high valuations.

summary: The Supreme Court appears likely to allow a class-action lawsuit against Nvidia to proceed, accusing the company of misleading investors about its reliance on cryptocurrency mining for revenue. This suit follows a 2022 SEC fine where Nvidia settled charges for failing to disclose crypto mining as a significant revenue source, despite not admitting wrongdoing. The case, alongside another involving Meta, highlights ongoing legal scrutiny on tech giants. | This article highlights three actively managed US ETFs that offer compelling investment opportunities: Dimensional US Core Equity 2 ETF (DFAC), Capital Group Dividend Value ETF (CGDV), and Avantis International Equity ETF (AVDE). These ETFs are lauded for their low fees, tax efficiency, and specific investment strategies such as factor tilts, dividend growth, and international diversification. The article suggests these actively managed ETFs offer advantages over traditional mutual funds for retail investors. | This article details the holdings of the JPMorgan U.S. Quality Factor ETF (JQUA), which was established in 2017 and primarily invests in large-cap equities. The ETF has $7,644.46 million in assets under management and 291 holdings, selected from the Russell 1000 based on profitability, earnings, and solvency. The document lists the top holdings by estimated value and recent changes in share counts for various companies within the ETF. | Warren Buffett, through Berkshire Hathaway, holds positions in two S&P 500-tracking ETFs, with the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF being highlighted for its low expense ratio. A top Wall Street analyst, Tom Lee of Fundstrat Global Advisors, predicts the S&P 500 could rise by 150% by 2030, driven by demographic shifts and the AI boom. The article emphasizes Buffett's advice for retail investors to opt for index funds over stock picking. | Amdocs Limited announced a record revenue of $5 billion for fiscal 2024, a 2.7% increase, and is strategically focusing on high-margin cloud services and generative AI for future growth. The company plans a 10% increase in quarterly dividends and expects pro forma revenue growth of 1% to 4.5% for fiscal 2025, driven by strong cloud adoption and ongoing operational efficiency. Amdocs is also phasing out low-margin, non-core business activities to sharpen its focus on strategic areas and improve profitability, targeting non-GAAP operating margins over 21% in fiscal 2025. | The article discusses the evolving landscape of AI regulation and its implications for marketers. It highlights the challenge for businesses to balance innovation with protecting consumer rights and maintaining trust, especially in the UK where regulatory approaches are still being defined. Key aspects covered include the need for robust AI infrastructure, data privacy, transparency, and the integration of brand values into AI strategies, emphasizing that self-governance and clear guidelines are crucial for navigating this new regulatory environment. | The Supreme Court is deliberating a challenge from Nvidia to a securities fraud lawsuit alleging the company misled investors about its sales dependence on volatile cryptocurrency miners. Justices appeared hesitant to set a broad rule, focusing instead on whether the plaintiffs met the legal bar for proceeding with a class action under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act. The outcome could significantly impact legal standards for similar lawsuits against corporations. | Cisco reported solid fiscal first-quarter financial results, beating analyst estimates for earnings and revenue, but saw a fourth successive quarter of declining revenue. Despite raising its 2025 full-year revenue outlook and highlighting growth in security and observability, the networking giant's stock traded lower after-hours due to investor disappointment over the overall revenue decline, especially in its core networking business. The company also emphasized its growing involvement in AI infrastructure orders and acquisitions of AI-focused security startups, though analysts remain skeptical about long-term growth strategies.
